content:
tess_acme (Customer): Hey support — over the last 6 hours a subset of our streaming requests to the hosted API are getting truncated mid-response. Dash shows the calls as 5xx and the billing page charged the full token amount even though the client dropped. Two recent request ids: rq_az987 and rq_bx123. Users see `broken pipe` in the client logs and truncated JSON chunks.

maria (Support): Thanks @tess_acme — sorry about this. Can you paste a minimal curl repro (no private prompt text) and confirm the region and API key mask? I'm escalating to eng-oncall (@alex). We'll also pull gateway logs for those request ids. :ear

`tess_acme (Customer):` sure — repro curl (uses client that reads stream and closes after first chunk):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-***" \\  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream \\  -d '{"model":"open-compat","prompt":"hello world","stream":true}' --no-buffer
```

maria (Support): I pulled partial gateway excerpt for rq_az987: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] gateway: proxy writev->upstream 10.4.2.7:443 id=rq_az987 status=200 bytes_sent=1421
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] gateway: writev: broken pipe id=rq_az987
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] gateway: classify: closing connection early -> labeled 502 id=rq_az987
```
That classification is why it shows as a 5xx and why billing counted it as server error path.

alex (Eng-Oncall): looks like this is our classic early-eof vs client-abort heuristic. Right now our gateway code maps an early `writev: broken pipe` during chunked transfer to a 502 if the server didn't explicitly send a final chunk header. In practice that mislabels customer-driven aborts (client closes after first chunk) as server 5xx.

Can you confirm: for rq_az987 did the upstream model respond with a 200 and at least one chunk before the socket closed? maria: logs show bytes_sent=1421 which implies at least one chunk made it out.

maria (Support): Correct — upstream returned 200 and we wrote data. The `bytes_sent` > 0. Yet classify->502 happened.

alex (Eng-Oncall): Ok. Proposed short-term mitigation: change classification so that if bytes_sent > 0 and upstream returned 2xx, then an `EPIPE`/`ECONNRESET` during response streaming is recorded as `client_disconnect` and not emitted as a 5xx metric or billed as a server error. We can roll that as a config tweak in the gateway logging/metrics. That should stop these from inflating 5xx and creating billing disputes.

raj (Infra): I can roll the config change to us-west-2 cluster in a canary (5% traffic) in ~10m. Note: metrics backfill won't change historical counts; we'll need to add an exception in billing pipeline to retroactively mark the two request ids as not-billed pending investigation.

maria (Support): @tess_acme we will issue a credit for rq_az987 and rq_bx123 while this is being fixed — filing billing-case #98765. Are there other request ids or times you can share? Also, can you try the same repro but set `--no-buffer` and then allow the client to stay connected to determine if the problem reproduces when the client keeps the socket open?

`tess_acme (Customer):` I can run that. Most of our clients do aggressive reconnects so it reproduces frequently. Appreciate the quick turnaround. 🙏

alex (Eng-Oncall): I'll open ENG-5432 for the code fix and link this thread. Fix plan:
- Change gateway heuristic: if upstream status is 2xx and bytes_sent > 0, treat EPIPE/ECONNRESET during response as client_abort (non-5xx).
- Add tracepoint to log `bytes_sent_at_abort` and `client-close-flags` to help debugging.
- Add unit + e2e that simulates client closing mid-chunked-stream.
- Add a metric `client_disconnect_after_first_chunk` to monitor regression.

Here's a quick grep command I used to fetch gateway lines for a request id:
```
kubectl logs gateway-abc -n prod | rg "rq_az987" -n
```
and to search for `EPIPE` across a time window:
```
rg "writev: broken pipe|EPIPE|upstream closed" /var/log/gateway/*.log | tail -n 50
```

raj (Infra): Rolling the canary now. Will post when done. ingress-bot:deploy started.

ingress-bot: deploy gateway-config v2026.03.15-canary -> us-west-2 (5% traffic) started by raj

raj (Infra): Canary completed, observing a drop in new `502-classify` counts for client-abort pattern in the canary subset. No perf regression noted. Rolling to 20% then 100% over 30m.

maria (Support): @tess_acme we added billing-case #98765 and put a provisional credit on those two request ids. Once ENG-5432 lands we'll follow up and keep you posted.

alex (Eng-Oncall): Follow-ups I put in the ticket: add an automated check to avoid counting these as 5xx in dashboards (so historical alerts don't re-fire), and add a small observability dashboard for `client_disconnect_after_first_chunk`. Also adding a regression test to the streaming e2e harness.

`tess_acme (Customer):` Thanks everyone — I'll test the repro against staging and report results in this thread. Appreciate the refund and the fast action. :raised_hands:

maria (Support): Closing the support thread for now; ENG-5432 and billing-case #98765 are open for tracking. Reopen if you see new ids after the rollout. cc @alex @raj
